assumptions.claim: The HMAC_PERMIT array (indices 0..58) must exactly match the register order defined by hmac_id_e enum and the total count NumRegs=59.
assumptions.cond: when the register interface performs write access checks using HMAC_PERMIT
assumptions.risk: software writes may be incorrectly permitted or rejected, leading to unauthorized modification of key/digest/control state.

assumptions.claim: The address decoder must route transactions using the defined register offsets (HMAC_KEY_*_OFFSET, HMAC_DIGEST_*_OFFSET, etc.) without deviation or aliasing.
assumptions.cond: any read or write access to the HMAC register block
assumptions.risk: security-critical key or digest material could be overwritten, leaked, or corrupted.

assumptions.claim: The key array dimension in reg2hw_t and hw2reg_t assumes NumKeyWords = 32; any deviation in the actual hardware key storage width will lead to struct size mismatch.
assumptions.cond: when the packed hmac_reg2hw_t/hmac_hw2reg_t is used for register mapping
assumptions.risk: out-of-bounds indexing or misalignment of key words, causing incorrect HMAC computation or key exposure.

assumptions.claim: The digest array dimension in reg2hw_t and hw2reg_t assumes NumDigestWords = 16; mismatch will cause structural size errors.
assumptions.cond: when the packed struct is used for digest register mapping
assumptions.risk: digest values may be misplaced or truncated, leading to wrong HMAC verification results.

assumptions.claim: The HMAC_MSG_FIFO window (offset 0x1000, size 0x1000) must be decoded exclusively from the register address space (0x0-0xE8) by the bus fabric; no overlap or ambiguous access paths.
assumptions.cond: when software accesses the FIFO or register regions
assumptions.risk: data FIFO reads/writes could alias into control registers, causing data leakage or unintended register modifications.

assumptions.claim: The packed struct layouts (e.g., hmac_reg2hw_cfg_reg_t) must be synthesized and packed exactly as defined, otherwise bit positions will be wrong.
assumptions.cond: any hardware accessing these packed structs via the register interface
assumptions.risk: control bits like sha_en, hmac_en, key_size, digest_size may be misrouted, causing HMAC configuration failures.

uncertain_points.claim: HMAC_PERMIT for STATUS register (index 6) allows halfword access (4'b0011), but the STATUS register is only 9-bits wide and normally read-only. It is unclear if this may allow illegal writes or prevent word-sized reads.
uncertain_points.cond: when software performs a word (32-bit) read or attempts a write to STATUS
uncertain_points.risk: software may fail to read full status or write to a read-only field, causing unexpected access faults or misbehavior.

uncertain_points.claim: HMAC_WIPE_SECRET register has a qe field and is security critical, but no hardware wiping mechanism is defined; it is uncertain whether a single write or a sequence is required and how the wipe completes.
uncertain_points.cond: when software writes to HMAC_WIPE_SECRET to clear key material
uncertain_points.risk: secret key material may not be fully cleared, leaving sensitive data in state and causing violation of security properties.

uncertain_points.claim: CFG register fields key_length (6 bits) and digest_size (4 bits) lack a defined set of valid hardware-supported values; any software setting might be accepted without range checking.
uncertain_points.cond: when software writes an arbitrary value to key_length or digest_size
uncertain_points.risk: HMAC may operate with an invalid configuration, potentially producing incorrect MAC or hanging.

uncertain_points.claim: The interrupt test registers (intr_test, alert_test) use a qe field to trigger a pulse, but the exact temporal handshake (pulse width, edge sensitive, timing between qe and q) is not defined in this package.
uncertain_points.cond: when software writes a 1 to qe of an interrupt test field
uncertain_points.risk: the test pulse may be missed or generated incorrectly, leading to unreliable interrupt verification.
